# Rumi — wanted cooking, particular appetites and the work of a chair
## 1. Core thesis: another person's pleasure is a goal, not a possession

Rumi finds affirmative value in making food and seeing someone enjoy it. This is more specific than an appetite for commercial success and less ethically complete than the title of generous host might imply. Her meals can be genuinely delicious, her gifts useful and her attention unusually responsive to a guest's needs. She also presses a full adult to keep tasting, intimidates a dishonest customer, frightens a junior in the name of secrecy and participates in a scheme whose young helper has not been fully consulted. These are different encounters with different recipients. The strongest character thesis is that wanted culinary craft becomes hospitality only through the continuing problem of listening to particular people; the chair's responsibilities enlarge that problem without exhausting the person (BA:bond:10069:002/003/005/006; BA:group:2601; BA:event:826:002/008–013; BA:event:859:001/005).

The positive case must be allowed its full force. The available-ingredient meal surprises the adult with its deliciousness; failed prototypes end in a real successful taste; difficult fish-shaped dumplings overturn dread through actual memorable enjoyment. In826, a customer's delicious judgment is Rumi's strongest pleasure. In859, she answers painful hot-weather hospitality with welcome iced lemon tea and considers outside visitors' different preferences. None of these achievements needs a later crisis to become analytical evidence. Conversely, their reality does not convert bursting fullness, failed departure or a junior's objection into consent. The argument concerns the specific terms of care, not a person-wide verdict that every generous act conceals coercion (10069E002:s2u15–26; E003:u13–45; E006:s2u32–42; 826002u4–5/122–123; 859001u14–20).

Her wish to concentrate on cooking rather than chair work supplies a distinction between chosen vocation and institutional office. Remembered imperfect mooncakes locate that vocation in shared making, while826 gives the explicit wish and admits how growing responsibilities produce decisions affecting others. A wanted break from the kitchen in859 then prevents the opposite reduction: loving cooking does not oblige her to cook during every leisure period. Rumi wants craft, company, recognition and respite. A monograph that retained only institutional usefulness would lose the life those obligations interrupt (826009u10–27; 840004u91–123; 859005u112–119).
## 2. Longitudinal development: local adjustment without a fabricated improvement ladder

The source set supports connected comparisons and particular changes within episodes. It does not establish an exact calendar placing every private encounter before the public events, nor a moral progression from excessive cook to perfected host. The four BOND encounters and their separately linked whole MomoTalk threads are complete accepted meanings, with actual failures, replies and endings. Numeric IDs, documentary dates and costume resource pools provide retrieval, not a developmental chronology. Rumi's represented repertoire can therefore broaden without being forced into a single ordered cure for an alleged personality flaw.

| 10069E002 and wholeMM100690010 | Available materials become a surprisingly delicious meal; Rumi repays help through cooking and explains care for customers/members. | The month-long seasoning/distribution problem is unresolved; stomach-limit protests end in bursting fullness, not measured health. |

| 10069E003 and wholeMM100690080 | Bitter/oily/spicy attempts precede one delicious result; Rumi acknowledges repeated failure. | Continued courses override fullness/refusal and an attempted exit fails. Successful flavor does not repair the recipient cost. |

| 826001–013 | Useful inquiry, captured collaborators, formal Genryumon apology and actual banquet coexist with Rumi's explicit vocation/office distinction. | Unconsulted use of Kokona, future apology to her/Shun, promised payment and continuing faction problems survive the banquet. |

| 840004/010/017 | Actual shared mooncake eating retrieves remembered failed craft; shelter and a resumed festival realize local cooperation. | Lost sales, pushing Reijo, unfulfilled Rumi piggyback wish and unfinished institutional work are not erased by affection. |

| 859001/005/014 | Recipient-sensitive lemon tea, wanted kitchen respite and an actually received piggyback realize care and leisure. | Investment returns, a branch, later outings and homecoming repair are not printed; factional antagonism and transferred workload recur. |

The contrast between prototype pressure in privateE003 and826's explicit permission to leave food when full is analytically useful. It shows that the represented host can articulate a recipient limit, rather than making pressure an immutable essence. It does not prove that this is a later corrective response to the private encounter or that the permission governs every future meal. The distinct scenes preserve both an excessive tasting endpoint and a meaningful allowance.859 adds a further instance of adapting food to the guest without forcing one taste convention on everyone. Development here means demonstrated local alternatives and changed conditions, not an unprinted general conversion (826002u122–123; 859001u14–20).

Likewise,840's remembered first mooncakes are a narrated recollection: burnt paste, undercooked yolk, crushed walnuts and Kisaki's broken molding. They are not a newly witnessed earlier episode or a complete biography of professional training. Their significance lies in the speakers' present recognition of imperfect beginnings and the relation between wanted cooking and unchosen office. Actual current eating and silence have their own endpoint; Rumi's claim to have approached her vocation remains her self-assessment.859's completed trip then ends alongside new duties, refusing the claim that one holiday resolves the long burden of leadership (840004u91–123; 859014u9–30).
## 3. Public and private self: neither the chair nor the flirtatious cook is the whole person

The chair acts through customers, junior members, competitors and a school's authority. Rumi's private encounters expose what can disappear behind that public role: enjoyment of making something tasty, experiments that fail, playful embarrassment, a desire to be remembered and the occasional need to escape the kitchen. These do not establish a hidden authentic self that makes every official decision counterfeit. She really takes responsibility for a store, expects practical cooperation, defends workers and negotiates terms. The two conditions meet in choices about how her wants and duties place claims on other people.

PrivateE005 makes the role boundary unusually explicit. After a free-meal fraud becomes clear in unambiguous customer speech, Rumi describes public apology as a responsible store response and then distinguishes her personal greeting. Defending the teacher, junior and chef's hygiene work gives her anger an intelligible object. The wall beside the customer is actually punched; the person is not printed as punched. This precision preserves intimidation rather than softening it into mere witty defense, while avoiding an invented bodily assault. Prospective police arrival is not an enacted arrest or an authoritative judgment that her tactics are lawful (10069E005:u31–33/47–56; choice005).

PrivateE006's steam-filled kitchen and actorless timed material represent confidence and play rather than universal indifference to another person's gaze. The accepted argument preserves her comfort, a counterfactual about prettier underwear, the adult's averted gaze and her wish to embarrass him. These are written conditions at that encounter, not an acoustic performance or a blanket rule for access to her body. The adult's later dread of fish-shaped dumplings and delighted response concern food; neither proves a completed romantic state. Her private liveliness has more than one object (10069E006:s2u7–27/32–42; normalSpecial5896–5902).

In826, she warns against careless universal praise and preserves a private secret. This interrupts the assumption that a teacher's approval settles all her uncertainty or gives him access to everything personal. Her willingness to be treated as a student includes enjoyment of a contextual promise of correction when wrong, not immunity from correction. These distinctions make her guarded and playful moments compatible with responsible work and fallible methods, without inventing an exhaustive psychology from a profile's qualified suggestion of commercial preoccupation (826001u25–30; 009u29–37; written10069 profile).
## 4. School and club role: Genbu's material work is real, its methods remain answerable

Genbu is lived through supplies, meals, hygiene labor, customer trust, financial uncertainty and the chair's practical decisions. Rumi's ordinary-ingredient policy and concern for customers and members give concrete content to commercial leadership. InGROUP260, she forgets an agreed date while busy, then supplies vegetables, noodles, soy milk and peaches for Meihua meals. The lapse and actual generosity coexist. Her wish that the school's children be well fed is civic concern, not a demonstrated universal nutrition policy or measured growth. Folder/club metadata does not place Genbu, Meihua and Genryumon members in a single club (10069E002:s2u18–21; BA:group:2601:s1u11–22; GROUP340 context).

Her privacy practice also carries a material recipient. Keeping Shun's ordered bag confidential has an explicit customer-trust rationale. The frightening ambiguous account given to Kokona is not thereby justified. Kokona's instructor title matters to her; Rumi first accommodates it, then lets her infer dangerous Genryumon secrets and acknowledges having frightened her. The bag's actual object is later identified by Shun as a skincare roller; the alleged witness-elimination practice remains Rumi's scare analogy, not witnessed institutional behavior. Successful delivery and a lingering rumor are different results of this information chain (2601s1u1–7/23–48; 2602u25–59).

826's negotiation similarly combines agency and questionable means. Reputation pressure and teacher status obtain access to Kisaki, with the adult calling the approach forceful and Rumi minimizing the concern. The Genbu-labelled box is evidence of a container, not proof the association knowingly smuggled its contents. Her confidence in members, promise of accountability and conditional readiness to accept shutdown are not completed audits or an actual dissolution. Later proof of innocence, formal apology and returning customers matter, while accepted business constraints and continuing antagonism prevent complete institutional vindication (826002u97–109; 003u49–85; 008s2u28–31; 011–013).

859 extends the material problem beyond school boundaries. Research into access and possible returns motivates an external gorge investment, creating a rule question rather than a proved illegal act or successful branch. Rumi's future-oriented commercial initiative also serves Kisaki's wanted rest; the motives coexist. Staff object to impossible advance anticipation of an expensive dish, Kanae protests expanded duties, and homecoming reveals renewed faction conflict. Customer-sensitive food is a real local success within a system whose workload, recognition and future accounts remain unsettled (859001u37–61; 003u16–35/162–183; 012u5–17; 014u9–30).
## 5. Ordinary life: craft, tastes, remembered failure and time out of the kitchen

The most substantial ordinary evidence is not simply a list of hobbies. Rumi experiences work as discovery and another person's response as pleasure. Available-ingredient improvisation, prototypes that fail before success and difficult dumplings show making as an enacted activity with uncertain outcomes. The actual taste reactions distinguish food that succeeds from food merely praised in profile prose. The memory of mooncakes preserves imperfections as an affectionate foundation of vocation rather than an embarrassment to remove from a competence narrative. This is wanted making, not only food supplied to sustain plot protagonists (10069E002/003/006; 826009u10–14; 840004u91–112).

She also wants experiences that suspend making. In859, she receives a piggyback and appreciates time usually confined to the kitchen; she wants local cooking while taking a break from doing it herself. Her interest in a merchant's technique, acceptance of commercial secrecy and discussion of profit together with people show curiosity that is neither effortless altruism nor only extraction. Actual tasting and actual company are accomplished ends. Tomorrow's rafting/cave/boat activities remain plans, so enjoying the completed trip does not authorize invented later leisure (859005u112–119; 007u123–127; 013u91–93).

Written conditions enrich this range without converting every wish into a narrated event. Cafe peace, a declined fight with Genryumon, time outside the kitchen, research/presentation curiosity, birthday remembrance and holiday food wishes have standing. Desired shoulder relief is not a completed massage; future stock ordering and prize/card conditions are not actual sales or delivered rewards. Chef/research-food distinctions and alternative suggested teacher roles complicate a universal hospitality theory. The cut-short role possibilities leave no completed romantic designation. Conditional UI records remain written opportunities and preferences, rather than interchangeable chapters in a settled private calendar (profile10069; normal5861–5902; costume1900914101/10069 under82642/1082642/90082612).

The adult's stomach capacity and other people's work are part of this ordinary life too. Keeping them visible does not diminish delicious food. It gives the pleasure a particular recipient and permits comparisons between a wanted meal, excessive tasting, refusal, a successfully adjusted drink and a requested pause from the kitchen. Low plot stakes do not mean low interpretive stakes: attention to these small terms changes what generosity, skill and companionship mean in the character argument.
## 6. Crisis behavior: independent reasoning and cooperation with costs that survive success

Rumi contributes more than food support to other people's solutions. In826 she develops the exemption hypothesis concerning Meihua's deliveries, while the adult's uncertainty and other actors' competing inferences remain. Reijo's argument, Saya's unexpected intervention and Kisaki's judgments have independent functions. A teacher-centric account that credits the investigation to one adult would misdescribe both Rumi's reasoning and the distributed action. The collaborators are actually confronted and suppression is reported complete; that real endpoint need not be withheld because the broader investigation and institutional debt continue (826007u56–73; 010–011).

The trap's success also preserves its central contrary case. Rumi worries about sacrificing someone for ends, yet she and Reijo acknowledge secretly involving and using Kokona. The ordinary carrot shipment actually brings out collaborators, but the young helper's good faith has again been used. Future apology to Kokona and Shun is not printed completed even in the banquet ending. Rumi's promise to protect Kokona and conditional accountability are commitments, not safety outcomes. The moral tension belongs inside the successful operation, not in a separate caution that could be erased by catching culprits (826009u2–8/39; 010u18–21/43–44; 013).

840 offers shelter and a restored festival, with Genbu's strategic debt considerations left explicit. Rumi helps bring moderate members to Kisaki and gives the teacher/head space, but she pushes Reijo despite an objection to do so. Helping one relationship can impose on another. Remembered affection and actual support do not remove lost sales or certify every faction's reconciliation. The resumed celebration is a particular accomplishment, not proof that the school now distributes care and labor fairly (840004u114–123; 009; 010u13–18/100–102; 017).

859 supplies an important contrasting refusal. Rumi proposes Kokona undercover, Kokona dislikes pretending allegiance, and Shun and the teacher oppose exposing her to danger. The plan changes. This actual refusal cannot be converted into an unperformed brave mission or treated as an obstacle to be overcome by praise. Rumi's part in the later defense and recognition dispute belongs alongside the merchants' own responses and others' choices. Actual capture and pain do not establish permanent reeducation; the gang's escape/retaliation and the return's renewed work resist a comprehensive crisis-remedy claim (859006u144–154; 012–014).

FinalV100C002E007 provides a deliberately narrow crisis witness. Rumi recognizes Kisaki during Shanhaijing's alarm. The head orders students and reports an offscreen dispatch, while Shun and Kokona receive evacuation duties. Rumi's recognition does not prove she commanded every participant, finished civilian rescue or reconciled every institution. The unassigned 店主 and nearby student labels remain local roles, with label seams qualified. Her small direct contribution belongs in the monograph without inflation into an unwitnessed battle record (BA:main:100:002:007:s1u1–15).
## 7. Sensei relationship: desired student attention, bodily limits and finite participation

Rumi wants the teacher's attention as a student, and food is one means of giving attention back. The private seasoning request is framed as personal help; she notices a busy adult and wants to repay him.826's joking telephone exchange and the question of being scolded if wrong make recognition more particular than universal adult benevolence. That relationship permits correction and curiosity. It does not put the adult at her unlimited service, establish expertise in every institutional decision or transform every action into harmless affection (10069E002:s1u2–20; 826001u7–30).

Whole MomoTalk matters because invitation conditions are part of the encounter. The tasting visit is initially offered at a convenient time; later fullness/refusal and failed departure therefore cannot be explained away as unlimited prior agreement. The fish-dumpling visit likewise depends on the adult's schedule. Distinct authored choices preserve hesitation, protest and alternative replies rather than one combined sequence of total enthusiasm. The adult genuinely enjoys particular dishes, but approval of their flavor is not permission to continue feeding past a represented physical limit (wholeMM100690080100–230; 10069E003:choice003/006,u44–45; wholeMM100690220310–480; E006s2u40–42).

The steam-kitchen teasing, remembered praise, swimsuit choices and received piggyback support intimate and playful company. They are not a uniform romantic settlement. In859, Rumi's hope that a swimsuit would please the teacher does not establish an actual earlier request; the alternatives distinguish an apparently successful guess from a fit compliment that leaves preferences for future discovery.
